questions.question: should I treat my boots out of box ? Annnnd how often should I treat them ?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** It depends on the boot. He says not to treat pretreated boots out of the box, but to condition rustic or distressed leather. After that he treats by feel, not on a fixed schedule. He mostly talks about Blundstones, so this is his advice for those. He hasn't covered other boot types here.

**Out of the box**
- **Pretreated boots:** In 2019 he read Blundstone's FAQ, which says most of their boots are pretreated and that they "do not recommend treating them out of the box". [1]
- **Rustic or distressed leather:** The exceptions are rustic brown, Crazy Horse and rustic black, which don't carry the same pretreatment as finished, oiled leather. [2] He says to treat these, "100%", and warns that conditioning will darken them. [3]
- **He changed his mind:** In his first Blundstone review (May 2019) he assumed his distressed pair was treated and water resistant. [4] About a week later he said that was wrong. [5]

**How often (his latest view, 2022)**
- **No set schedule:** He says he does it when he feels the boots need it and that he probably does too little. He also says other people are more regimented. [6]
- **Signs it's time:** The leather looks or feels dry, or water isn't beading on top. Dry-looking leather needs oil, and poor beading means more wax. [7]
- **Clean them regularly:** He says dirt wears the leather down faster. [7]
- **Order:** Clean, then condition, then wax. [8]
- **Heavy use:** In his 2019 review he said you may have to wax every month, or maybe every week if you go super crazy with your boots. [9]
- **Leather you've neglected:** He says any leather you haven't conditioned in a few months should definitely be conditioned. [3]

questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
**Yes, the first soak or wash makes them tighter, mostly in the waist, but they loosen again with wear.** His advice is to size up when you buy them.

**Sizing (his newest view):**
- In 2025 he says you should usually go two sizes up in a shrink-to-fit 501 [1].
- In 2021 he says Levi's advice is correct: size up two in the waist and two inches in length, and the pants will then fit regularly once wet [2].
- He used to ignore that advice. In 2019 he says he "didn't listen to Levi at all" [3]. By 2021 he says it took him four pairs of 501s to realize Levi's was right [2].

**How much they tighten:**
- In 2019 he soaked a pair and said they "definitely did slim up," mainly in the waist, while the length barely changed [4][5].
- In 2020 he says that when he first got his pair in his normal size, he could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe [6].

**They stretch back out:**
- A week after soaking his 2019 pair, he says the upper thigh and waist had stretched enough to wear a belt [7].
- In 2023 he says that if you wear them frequently, he bets they would stretch out to about the same size as a regular rinsed pair [8].

**Washing tip:** In 2023 he says not to put them in very hot water or the dryer, because that is what makes them much smaller. He says that without that, you can get a really nice fit [9].

He hasn't said how much they keep shrinking in washes after the first soak.

questions.question: I'm usually a 33x30 in Levi's 502s, what size should I buy in these? [501 STF]

hybrid.answer:
Applying his rule to your size, he would point you to about a **35 waist x 32 length** in the 501 STF. He hasn't talked about 502s, so that's his general sizing advice applied to your numbers, not something he said about your fit.

**His rule (most recent view):** In 2025 he says you "should usually go two sizes up" on the 501 STF [1]. In 2021 he gave the full version: Levi's advice is two sizes up in the waist and two inches more in length, and "if you usually wear a 34 get a 36". He added that he doesn't think a 36 exists, so he doesn't say what to do when the size isn't made, and he doesn't say whether a 35 is available [2]. In 2023 he bought size 32 jeans when he's a 30 [3]. For you, that rule gives 35 x 32.

**He used to ignore this advice.** In 2019 he skipped Levi's advice and bought his usual 29 waist and 30 length [4]. A year later he said he could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe, though he liked the fit once they stretched, and he said he would definitely have bought a 32 length [5]. By 2021 he said it took him four pairs of 501s to realize "levi's is correct and that's what you should do" [2]. So he began by ignoring the sizing advice and ended up recommending it.

**Shrinking:** He says to avoid very hot water and the dryer, and then "you can get a really nice fit" [6].

questions.question: Why do you cuff your jeans?

hybrid.answer:
He cuffs mainly to deal with length and width. His latest word (2020) is that he cuffed his Levi's 501s because his current style doesn't suit wider-legged pants left uncuffed. He has also hedged: by late 2019 he said he liked jeans over his boots more than cuffing.

**Most recent (2020, Levi's 501 STF):** He cuffed the 501s "just because i don't think my current style kind of lends itself to not cuffed wider legged pants." [1] He also says he would have bought a 32 length. [2]

**Late 2019 (L.L. Bean boots):** He says he always used to cuff his jeans but now likes them over his boots a little bit more. [3]

**Mid 2019 (first Levi's 501 video):** Length matters most to him. He says it's all about length, that jeans look bad if they look too long, and that the cuff can't be too thick. [4]

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** He used to say yes, but by September 2023 he hedged. He calls the 3335s his favorite Red Wings "of all time" and says they "still might be," but probably not, and he was selling them.

**Most recent (Sept 2023):** He says he's on record calling the 3335s his favorite Red Wings, then hedges: "they still might be but they probably not." He adds that the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes [1]. He likes the 3335s because they're stitch-down and lighter, so he can feel more nimble and walk or do a light hike in them [2]. Even so, he says they're going from his collection [2].

**Oct 2022:** At that point he was clear. The 3335s were his favorite boots he'd ever had, and he said they beat the 1907s and 875s [3]. His reasoning was that he's hiking and walking in the woods rather than doing heritage work. He called the 3335s a dramatically better all-around boot for that [3]. He also likes the Vibram mini lug sole on the 3335s over the crepe soles on the 875s and 1907s [5]. He added that the 1907s and 875s are more beefily built, so if you need a tough boot, the 3335s are probably not the ones to go for [4].

**Sept 2021:** Before the 3335s, he recommended the 1907s. He said that if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing, you should get the 1907s [6].

questions.question: How do you feel bout blunnies as of Late 2023?

hybrid.answer:
As of his latest video here (September 2023), he is still a big Blundstone fan, but he is retiring his much-worn 585s and letting go of his heavy-duty Extremes as part of cutting down his boot collection.

**September 2023 (collection cull)**
- He says Blundstones are "just incredible" and that he has "always loved them" [1].
- His beaten-up 585s, the subject of his first-ever video, have "held up through it all" and stayed "probably my most water resistant boots" [1].
- Even so, he says it's "time to retire those bunnies" [2].
- The heavy-duty Extreme work boots he calls "insane boots", but he says they have to go [3][4]. He also says they are only very water-resistant nubuck, not waterproof [3].
- These decisions are about thinning the collection, not a verdict against the brand.

**Earlier views, for context**
- In 2022 he asked whether Blundstones are still worth it. He wrote "All in all I love Blundstones!" and said they're not as repairable as Goodyear-welted boots like Red Wings or Wolverines, but are still some of his favorites [5].
- In 2019 he called them "by far my favorites" of his three or four boots, as long as you keep the leather treated [6].

So his view hasn't soured since 2019. He has simply decided to move on from the pairs he owned.

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
He consistently favours Solovair for value. In his 2022 comparison he says Solovair is the cheaper, better-built choice, and he later softens that only a little about his own pair (see below). By 2023 he still likes his Solovair monkey boots and says Made in England Docs are only really for big Dr. Martens fans.

**Where he lands (2022)**
- On materials he calls them roughly even: the Made in England leather is "probably on par with solar bears" [1]. He says the midsoles are probably on par too [1].
- Solovairs are cheaper than Made in England Docs [2].
- Solovair boots have a shank, so he says they're a bit more comfortable over long periods [3][4]. Docs have none [5].
- He says they're Goodyear welted in a more regularly accepted way, so they're easier to resole [4].
- He calls the Solovair derby eight-eyed boot essentially the same boot as Doc Martens, from the original maker [6].
- The one thing Solovair doesn't do is the yellow stitching. If that matters to you, he says you have to get the Made in England Docs [7].
- He argues that much of the roughly third extra you pay for Made in England is the "made in England" part itself, which is why he'd rather you buy Solovair for pure value [8].

**Caveats on Solovair**
- His own pair had a manufacturing defect: a ripped back tab and a snapped lace after eight wears. He still says he loves them [9].
- In September 2023 he said he still really likes the monkey boots despite the quality-control issue and Solovair's handling of it [10].
- He finds the fit loose, which he thinks probably means he sized wrong. He'd sell them only to buy another pair of monkey boots [10].

**Made in England on its own (2023)**
- He says the $260 Made in England 1460 is probably not worth the extra $90 on a purely robotic view. They suit big fans who want boots made the old way [11].
- He says you'd have to be a mega fan to get them [12].

He hasn't directly compared the two again since the 2022 video.

questions.question: Hi, I am going on a 4 day hike and I am wondering if I can use my blundstone for them, what do you think?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** He hasn't talked about multi-day hikes, so there's no direct verdict. Going by what he has said, Blundstones are a risky pick for a 4-day hike, mainly because of ankle support and break-in.

**Ankle support:** After wearing his pair up and down mountains in Maine, he said they "are not good boots for mountaining apparently because they don't have uh good ankle support" [1]. They still did the job for him: he "got them a little scuffed up and they held up well" [2].

**Break-in:** If yours aren't fully broken in, be careful. He got "big fat gross blisters like break-in blisters for boots" once he started running and walking the track in them, and they stopped after two to three weeks [3]. In his first review he had no blisters walking around a city and woods in a brand-new pair [4].

**Not a tough-use boot:** He calls them "decent for work boots but not anything incredible" [5]. He says they're fine if you're "crossing a brook or a stream" or standing in mud for a bit [6].

**Water resistance:** This matters over several days. They're water resistant, not waterproof, and that depends on keeping them treated. He says to buy them "knowing that you'll have to take care of them" [7]. By 2023 his heavily worn pair had "remained probably my most water resistant boots through it all" [8].

**What he hasn't covered:** Carrying a pack, long distances over several days, and how Blundstones compare with real hiking boots for this. If you do take them, his advice points to treating them beforehand and making sure they're broken in.

questions.question: I'm 5'11-225 lbs with a dad bod. What's the most cost efficient and quality t shirt for me? Also, what size would u prefer?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** Start with the Uniqlo tee, but for your height and weight he'd steer you to the Muji tee. He hasn't said what size you should buy.

**Best value (his latest view, Sept 2025)**
- He says the $20 Uniqlo tee is probably the best t-shirt you can get "bar none for the price" [1]. He calls it a starter tee, but adds that if you're taller or wider you'd want Muji instead [2].
- Muji costs about $4–5 more, but it's "significantly longer and a good deal wider." He says that if you're a little bigger you'd probably like it [3]. Earlier in 2025 he also said the Muji feels justified at about $10 more than Uniqlo, with a thicker, tighter collar and a nicer feel [4].

**Other value picks if you'll spend a bit more**
- **House of Blanks ($35, made in Canada):** He found zero torque (twisting) and called it a truly outstanding value [5].
- **Front General Store ($40, made in Japan):** He praises its proportions and feel [6].
- **Bronson:** He says Bronson usually wins or comes close in t-shirt comparisons [7]. In mid-2025 he rated Bronson ($29) and Bravestar ($32) slightly above Uniqlo for value [8].

**Cheapest option:** In 2024 he said the Costco Kirkland six-pack is quite long and that he can't recommend it enough if you want a shirt under $5–6 [9][10].

**Size**
He hasn't given a size for a 5'11", 225 lb build, so I can't name one for you. What he does say:
- He likes a lot of space across the shoulders and shirts that "flatten me out" [11][12].
- Brands run differently. He thinks the Los Angeles Apparel tee might win if you size down one [13].
- For you, that points to Muji's extra width and length, and to a roomier fit rather than a tight one.

questions.question: Am I the only one who loves these videos but in the end still has no idea which to buy? Please just tell me: buy this one, or these 3. I can't decide between 25 options. [t-shirts]

hybrid.answer:
He never names one shirt to buy, and he says there isn't one: by 2025 he says every shirt he's covered is a winner and the best one depends on your preferences. In 2024 he did crown a single overall winner, Asket [1][2]. His simplest answers are below.

**If you want just one, with no fuss:** Uniqlo at $20. He calls it "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" and says it's the starter tee. If you're taller or wider, he says to get Muji instead, which is a few dollars more but longer and wider [3][4].

**If you want 3, his own 2025 picks are:**
- **J. Press x American Trench** is his pick for an all-around tee. He likes its rougher hand feel and structure [5].
- **Front General Store** is his pick for best value, and he says he's feeling it "today". It has more character, and he says he might pick House of Blanks (perfectly smooth, no torque) another day [6].
- **Merz b. Schwanen 2M15** is his pick for an elevated, minimalist tee, though he says Lady White could be his favorite and all of them are great choices [6].

**Other category picks:**
- For Japanese tees, he'd go with Wonder Looper over Samurai, because of its more universal fit [7].
- For heavyweights, he picks American Giant "by a long shot", because it's lighter and fits more universally [7].

**The 2024 verdict:** In his 2024 roundup he named Asket the winner, the silkiest, densest and most interesting shirt [2]. In 2025 he says Asket is still very high up, but it left the final list because that list only covered shirts under $50 [8].

questions.question: 1907 vs the 875's? What's the difference?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** the 1907 and the 875 are close, and in 2021 he picked the 1907 as the better buy. The main differences are the welt, the extras, and about $10 in price. Since then he has moved away from a clear winner. In 2022 he said his favorite boots are the 3335s, which beat both. In 2023 he said the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers each have characteristics he really likes.

**His verdict over time**
- 2021: he says to get the 1907 if you're looking at a moc toe Red Wing. [1]
- 2022: he says the 3335s beat both the 1907s and 875s for his hiking and walking use. He adds that the 1907s and 875s are more beefily constructed, so you'd pick those if you need a tough boot. [7][8]
- 2023: he says the 875s, 1907s and Iron Rangers all have their own characteristics that he really likes. [9]

**Welt construction**
- The 875 is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts durable and pretty water resistant, and the welt leaves room for a cork footbed that molds to your foot. [2][3]
- The 1907 has a storm welt, which Red Wing sometimes calls Norwegian-like. [1] He relays the popular Reddit view that Red Wing just stitches another strip of leather onto the welt, but says "i'm not quite sure". [4]

**Price and extras**
- The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875. [5]
- He says that gets you the storm welt, which he finds invaluable, a removable leather footbed (about $40 separately) and leather laces thrown in. [6]
- He argues the extras make the 1907 the better deal. [6]

**Soles**
- Both have crepe soles, which he says he doesn't really like. He thinks they break down faster than the Vibram lug sole on the 3335. [7][10]

**Water resistance**
- In his waterproof test on the 1907, the right boot leaked almost immediately through the stitching, while the left stayed dry. [11]
- He still has no doubt it would hold up fine in rain, grass or mud. [11]
- He hasn't tested the 875 in the videos available here.

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** he picks Uniqlo as the best-value tee for the money, and Front General Store as the upgrade he personally favors. Hanes and Pro Club are the cheap classics he rates lower on softness.

**Uniqlo (his newest, strongest value pick):** In his September 2025 roundup he says the $20 Uniqlo tee is "probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. He calls it a rough, open-ended "starter t-shirt" [2]. Earlier in 2025 he praised its bound neck collar and said the price-to-quality ratio is insane [4]. In 2024 he said the Uniqlo heavyweight crew "may be" the best bargain tee [9].

**Front General Store:** He says it is a $40, 100% made-in-Japan shirt with "Great proportions, great feel" [3]. In 2024 he called it "one of the best shirts that you could possibly get" if you want a Japan-made upgrade under about $40. He gave it a softness of 6 out of 10 [6]. In 2025 he again called it a really good tee at about $38 [5]. When he picked a favorite in the best-value category, he said "Today I'm feeling the Front General Store" [7]. He added that he might pick House of Blanks another day.

**Pro Club:** He liked it. In 2024 he said "all in all I like everything about it," but he described it as the roughest shirt on that list and gave it a softness of 4 out of 10 [8]. He hasn't put it above Uniqlo or Front General Store in the videos available here.

**Hanes:** In 2024 he called it "your classic $10 great shirt" and gave it a softness of 7 out of 10 [10]. In 2025 he lumped "Hannes and Gild" in with the very cheap mass-market brands [11]. Of five shirts from those brands, he said all had a defect [12]. That lumping is loose, so I wouldn't read it as a Hanes-only verdict.

**Bottom line:** For the least money and the best overall value, he points to Uniqlo. If you can spend about $40 and want a Japan-made tee with more character, he leans Front General Store. If you're taller or wider, he suggests Muji instead of Uniqlo for the extra length and width [13].

questions.question: Would you recommend this or the flint and tinder for someone who would use it like a rain jacket but also a windbreaker and a spring light jacket?

hybrid.answer:
I can't tell what "this" refers to. He hasn't ranked jackets for that exact rain, wind and spring mix, so the clearest comparison is the Barbour from the same video. For a rain, wind and light-spring jacket, the Barbour's features fit better, while the Flint and Tinder is the easier all-round pick.

**Flint and Tinder Waxed Trucker (2025)**
- He says it is built for everyone [1]. It isn't crazy lightweight but is a lighter weight, so it's comfortable [1].
- He says it is lined, so you don't get wax on your skin [2]. He also calls it hard not to recommend at $300, because it is US-made, lined and uses Martexin wax canvas [3].
- That segment was sponsored by Huckberry, but he says he had talked about the jacket many times before being sponsored [4].
- In his 2023 jacket comparison he described the Huckberry trucker as unlined and the lightest fabric of that group, wearable when it's a little warmer out [5]. He says in 2025 that it's lined, so the lining is the newer word.
- He doesn't say anything about the Flint and Tinder's rain or wind performance, or about hoods and cuffs.

**Barbour (2025, his top pick in the voting)**
- It uses 6 oz Sylkoil, the lightest fabric in that video [6]. He says you could wear it any time of year and be super comfortable [7].
- It has a throat latch, snaps for a hood, vents [8], and storm cuffs, which he calls really helpful in inclement weather [9].
- He notes it's not a designated rain jacket, and that for him this means the fabric is lightweight [10].

**Bottom line:** For rain and wind use plus a light spring layer, his comments point to the Barbour, since it has the hood snaps and storm cuffs. The Flint and Tinder is the simpler everyday jacket. If you tell me which jacket "this" is, I can compare more directly, but he hasn't spoken to that specific pairing.

questions.question: Do you know how these fit compared to the 875s? [Red Wing 3335s]

hybrid.answer:
He hasn't directly compared the fit of the 3335s to the 875s in the videos available here, but he gives a few related points. He took the 3335s true to size, and they run slimmer and more tapered than you might expect.

**3335 fit:** He went true to size and says they fit fine [1]. The profile is slim because the outsole is very thin and the boots taper down. With thin cotton socks he had no tightness, but with wool socks his toes feel squished and he can't wiggle them much [2].

**875s:** He doesn't describe the 875's fit on its own. In his 1907 video he says he usually wears an 8 in boots, bought an 8 in Red Wings, and they fit perfect. He adds that leather boots should be bought snug, not squished [3]. That video covers the 1907, not the 875 or 3335, so it only loosely applies. He does describe the 875s and 1907s as more beefily constructed than the 3335s [4].

**Bottom line:** From his comments, true to size works for the 3335s. Expect a slimmer, tapered toe area, especially if you wear wool socks. He hasn't said whether the 875s are roomier.
